correctness.rationale: The selected-edge graph in K_{m,n} faithfully represents open-neighborhood domination on K_m square K_n. Undominated cells are the product of untouched row/column vertices together with isolated selected-edge components. A legal edge joining only previously used endpoints must meet an isolated edge and cannot create a cycle, giving the forest invariant. At first exhaustion of one side, remaining steps destroy isolated edges, proving upper bound m+n-2 except the m by (m+1) matching case with m+n-1; the explicit row/column star sequence and saturated matching plus attachments realize both. The duality with skew zero forcing is a known identity, not a second new proof. Source proof covers all m,n>=2; finite verification is not used to infer the all-dimension claim.
